notes:
- One header per screen: Settings sub-screens no longer stack their titles: opening a part of Interface or Theme used to leave the page's header, the part's header and the part's own sub-header on screen at once, so three rows of title pushed the first control below the fold. Card design's three parts are now peers of the Card design shelf rather than a third level inside it, and the screen you are on draws the only header. Back still walks out one level at a time.
- Card names and scores are on by default again: 2.3.1 shipped both switches off while its release notes said "both are on by default, so no card changes until you ask" - so every grid silently lost its caption on upgrade. They are on now, matching the shipped build before the switch existed; turn either off in Card design > Poster art when the artwork already carries the name or the score.
- The Library view keeps its own grid: Card size no longer adds or removes a column, which is how choosing Compact under Big cards drew three across in a two-up view. The Library view's own count wins - Big cards stays two, Cover wall and Poster grid three, Shelf five - and card size now changes the cover's proportions instead. Cover wall and Shelf keep their caption-free strips whatever the card design says.
- Clean BetterPosters, and a preview of what you get: A fresh install now asks btttr for the clean poster: the artwork and the show's name, with the score, the genre line and the trend strip all off by default. Card design > Poster art draws a live sketch of the poster above the three switches, so turning one on shows exactly what appears on the picture. The show's name is part of every btttr variant - including poster-n - so that one stays, while the app's own caption has its own switch underneath.
- Sequel seasons stop repeating one poster: btttr addresses a poster by IMDb series, and every season of a show shares that entry - so Frieren Season 2 and Season 3 both drew Season 1's picture under a different name. Unique art for sequels is on by default: a title that names Season 2, 3rd Season, Part 2 or Final Season keeps its own AniList cover, which is season-specific and usually carries that season's name in the art. Turn it off in Poster art to use the series poster everywhere; the season check understands the spellings AniList actually uses and never treats a year like 2049 as a season.
- Dark mode is one tap away: The Light / Dark / System tiles moved out of the Appearance sub-page and onto the Theme shelf, directly under the live preview - the mode is the first thing this page is for, and it no longer costs a screen to reach. The Appearance row is gone. OLED mode and the canvas colours keep their own Background row, which is all that sub-page now contains.
- UI size belongs with reading: The UI size presets and the exact-dpi slider moved from Interface > App layout to Type & reading, beside the text scale. They answer the same question - how large the app is drawn - and a reader looking for a bigger app now finds both in the page named for reading, instead of inside a card about the shelf and the bar.
- Colour from the poster you actually see: The theme seed is now read from the picture on screen: with BetterPosters on, the colour comes from btttr's rendered art rather than the AniList cover, so the sheet, its backdrop and its tint belong to the poster the reader is looking at. The quantizer also returns a second, distinct hue from the same pixels, and the hero's backdrop and the page wash use it as a gradient instead of one flat colour. The decode is 96px and cached in pairs, so the extra colour costs one pass, not two.
- Blur that costs nothing when it is off: Crisp used to apply a zero-radius blur, which still renders the image through an offscreen layer. The Info page and the appearance preview now skip the layer entirely at Crisp and only pay for the blur they can see. The appearance preview also draws the poster source you chose - BetterPosters included - instead of always previewing the AniList cover, so the sample matches the app you have.
- Deeper descriptions on the Interface pages: Library view explains what the selected mode does to the grid and the caption, Card shape says plainly that size changes the cover's proportions and not the column count, and Poster art separates what btttr burns into the picture from what the card draws underneath it - including the one thing btttr cannot remove.
- Sequels the name does not give away: Sequel detection only recognised a season when the title said Season 2, 3rd Season, Part 2 or Final Season, so Nisemonogatari - season 2 of the same IMDb series as Bakemonogatari - kept the shared btttr poster. The app now also reads the season ARM reports for the IMDb mapping and keeps the AniList cover for anything past season one, which covers sequels whose names never mention a number.
- A dissolve instead of a snap: Changing the app layout in Settings swapped the whole Home screen in one frame, which read as a reload. Nova and Classic now crossfade through the same motion tokens as the rest of the app - instant when Motion is set to Instant - and a poster crossfades when BetterPosters arrives or the poster source changes, instead of flickering between the two images.
